title: Nudge-token equality guard reverts even when nudge is size-disabled
description: The up-front equality guard (lines 230-233) reverts whenever nudgePaymentToken != 0 && nudgePaymentToken == paymentToken, unconditionally on nudgeSize, BEFORE the nudgeSize gate at lines 245-246. So even when the nudge is disabled via nudgeSize == 0 (no payout would occur), a configured-but-equal nudge token bricks every batchMint. Confirmed unchanged at HEAD 031ffda.
impact: None. QA/usability nit: batchMint reverts for a config (nudge token == payment token) that is harmless when nudgeSize == 0. Spec-vs-behavior mismatch (overbroad guard), no asset risk, no availability impact in any intended operating mode.
attackPath: 1. Owner config has nudgePaymentToken == paymentToken with nudgeSize == 0 (nudge disabled).
2. Every batchMint reverts despite no payout being possible - an overbroad guard / spec-vs-behavior mismatch.
recommendation: Gate the equality guard on nudgeSize != 0 (only enforce nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken when a nudge payout can actually occur).

mergedSourceIds: carried forward from ledger; confirmed at HEAD 031ffda
